- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- When true outcome shows sharp drop after a spike, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast peak height by 5–10% in next period.  
- If model forecast is flat or slowly rising while sentiment is negative, force a downward adjustment of 2–5% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to align with mean reversion behavior.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 75.00 after 10+ days, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 2–3% to account for lagged market reaction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model should not assume trend continuation — apply conservative, flat or slightly downward adjustment.
